children: Shares of Copa Holdings jumped 5.1% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter financial results showing year-over-year growth in operating revenue and earnings per share.

According to the company's earnings release, Copa Holdings' third-quarter operating revenue increased 31.9% year over year, while revenue per available seat mile (RASM) rose 13.5% compared to the third quarter of 2025. The release also showed net profit of $175.8 million, or $4.29 per share, a 2.2% year-over-year increase in earnings per share, while operating margin decreased 4.6 percentage points to 18.6% and net margin fell 4.4 percentage points to 14.6% from the third quarter of 2025.

Copa Holdings reported that capacity, measured in ASMs (available seat miles), increased 16.3% year over year and passenger traffic in RPMs (revenue passenger miles) rose 17.1%, lifting load factor—the share of available seating capacity filled—by 0.7 percentage points to 88.7%, amid significantly higher jet fuel prices.
What is the market telling us

Copa Holdings’s shares are quite volatile and have had 18 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Copa Holdings is up 16.8% since the beginning of the year, but at $142.36 per share, it is still trading 9.4% below its 52-week high of $157.19 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Copa Holdings’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,812.
